taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Standard set, reasoning allowed. Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Reasoning: September 30, 2026 is during EDT (UTC-4). Madrid in late September is on CEST (UTC+2). Difference is 6 hours. 5:00 PM ET → 11:00 PM Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima is UTC-5 (no DST), so 12:00 UTC = 07:00 local.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST is UTC+2. Japan is UTC+9. Difference is 7 hours ahead.

9:00 AM CEST = 16:00 JST on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PDT is UTC-7. Madrid in October is on CEST (UTC+2) until the last Sunday of October (Oct 25, 2026), so Oct 12 is still CEST.

Oct 11, 2026 23:59 PDT = Oct 12, 2026 06:59 UTC = Oct 12, 2026 08:59 CEST.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PST is UTC-8. March 3, 2026 11:59 PM PST = March 4, 2026 07:59 UTC.

Madrid in early March is on CET (UTC+1), so 07:59 UTC = 08:59 Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1. 10:00 AM CET = 09:00 UTC. Los Angeles in February is on PST (UTC-8), so 09:00 UTC = 01:00 AM PST on February 2, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

JST is UTC+9, Lima (PET) is UTC-5, so difference is 14 hours.

May 5, 2026 8:00 AM JST = May 4, 2026 6:00 PM Lima time.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Reasoning: October 28, 2026 is after US DST ends? No, US DST ends November 1, 2026. So PT = PDT = UTC-7. Spain: CEST ends October 25, 2026, so Madrid is on CET = UTC+1 on October 29. Difference: PDT to Madrid = +8 hours.

11:59 PM PDT Oct 28 + 8 hours = 7:59 AM Oct 29 Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Reasoning:
- October 30, 2026: US is still on EDT (DST ends Nov 1, 2026), so ET = UTC-4.
- Spain: DST ends Oct 25, 2026, so Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.
- 9:00 AM EDT = 13:00 UTC = 14:00 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1. However, I need to check if CET actually applies on October 27, 2026, or if Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) is in effect.

In Europe, DST ends on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, that's October 25. So by October 27, 2026, Europe will be on standard time (CET, UTC+1).

New York on October 27, 2026 will still be on EDT (UTC-4), since US DST ends on the first Sunday of November (November 1, 2026).

So: 18:00 CET = 17:00 UTC = 13:00 EDT.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Reasoning: November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT. In early November, US has already ended DST (Nov 1, 2026), so PT = PST = UTC-8. Spain ends DST on last Sunday of October (Oct 25, 2026), so Madrid is on CET = UTC+1. Difference: 9 hours ahead.

11:59 PM PST Nov 2 + 9 hours = 8:59 AM Nov 3 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Reasoning:
- March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT. In March, US has already switched to PDT (DST began March 8, 2026), so PT = PDT = UTC-7.
- 11:59 PM PDT = 06:59 UTC on March 21, 2026.
- Spain in March 2026: DST begins March 29, 2026, so on March 21 Madrid is still on CET = UTC+1.
- 06:59 UTC + 1 = 07:59 Madrid time on March 21, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1. On March 25, 2026, Europe is on CEST (UTC+2), but the problem states CET explicitly, so I'll use UTC+1.

12:00 CET = 11:00 UTC. Los Angeles on March 25, 2026 is on PDT (UTC-7), so 11:00 UTC = 04:00 PDT.

However, if "CET" is being used loosely to mean the current Central European time (which would be CEST in late March), then 12:00 would be UTC+2 = 10:00 UTC = 03:00 PDT.

I'll go with the literal interpretation of CET = UTC+1.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026 = 00:00 EDT (UTC-4) since DST is still in effect in October.

That's 04:00 UTC on October 12, 2026.

Madrid in October is on CEST (UTC+2), so 04:00 UTC = 06:00 Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) = UTC-12. So deadline is Oct 9, 2026 23:59 UTC-12 = Oct 10, 2026 11:59 UTC.

Madrid in October is on CEST (UTC+2) until the last Sunday of October (Oct 25, 2026). So Oct 10 is still CEST = UTC+2.

11:59 UTC + 2 = 13:59 Madrid time on Oct 10, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PT in August is PDT (UTC-7). 12:00 PM PDT = 19:00 UTC.

Madrid in August is CEST (UTC+2) = 21:00.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

IST (Indian Standard Time) is UTC+5:30.
Deadline: Nov 10, 2026, 23:59 IST = Nov 10, 2026, 18:29 UTC.

Madrid in November is on CET (UTC+1).
18:29 UTC + 1 = 19:29 Madrid time on Nov 10, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nepal time is UTC+5:45. Lima is UTC-5 (no DST).

5:00 PM Nepal = 17:00 - 5:45 = 11:15 UTC on April 2, 2026.
Lima: 11:15 - 5:00 = 06:15 on April 2, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Adelaide in October is on daylight saving time (ACDT, UTC+10:30).
Madrid in October (before last Sunday) is on CEST (UTC+2). October 6, 2026 is before the last Sunday (Oct 25), so Madrid is UTC+2.

10:00 AM ACDT = 23:30 previous day UTC = 01:30 Madrid time (next day... wait).

10:00 Oct 6 ACDT - 10:30 = 23:30 Oct 5 UTC
23:30 UTC + 2:00 = 01:30 Oct 6 Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney on Oct 3, 2026: AEDT started Oct 5, 2025... wait, let me check. Australian DST: AEDT begins first Sunday of October. In 2026, first Sunday of October is Oct 4. So on Oct 3, 2026, Sydney is still on AEST (UTC+10).

6:00 PM AEST = 08:00 UTC on Oct 3, 2026.

Madrid: CEST ends last Sunday of October (Oct 25, 2026). So on Oct 3, Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2).

08:00 UTC = 10:00 Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
